verses.speaker: धृतराष्ट्र
verses.devanagari:
धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः ।
मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत संजय
verses.iast:
dharmakṣetre kurukṣetre samavetā yuyutsavaḥ |
māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāścaiva kimakurvata saṃjaya
verses.meaning: The blind king Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya: what did my sons and Pandu's sons do when they gathered to fight on the holy field of Kurukshetra?
verses.takeaway: Every story starts with an honest question.

verses.speaker: सञ्जय
verses.devanagari:
दृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवानीकं व्यूढं दुर्योधनस्तदा ।
आचार्यमुपसंगम्य राजा वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
dṛṣṭvā tu pāṇḍavānīkaṃ vyūḍhaṃ duryodhanastadā |
ācāryamupasaṃgamya rājā vacanamabravīt
verses.meaning: Sanjaya answers: seeing the Pandava army drawn up for battle, Prince Duryodhana went to his teacher Drona and spoke.
verses.takeaway: Look at the field before you speak.

verses.devanagari:
पश्यैतां पाण्डुपुत्राणामाचार्य महतीं चमूम् ।
व्यूढां द्रुपदपुत्रेण तव शिष्येण धीमता
verses.iast:
paśyaitāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāmācārya mahatīṃ camūm |
vyūḍhāṃ drupadaputreṇa tava śiṣyeṇa dhīmatā
verses.meaning: Duryodhana says: O teacher, look at this mighty Pandava army, drawn up by your clever pupil, Drupada's son.
verses.takeaway: Give credit where it is due — even to rivals.

verses.devanagari:
अत्र शूरा महेष्वासा भीमार्जुनसमा युधि ।
युयुधानो विराटश्च द्रुपदश्च महारथः
verses.iast:
atra śūrā maheṣvāsā bhīmārjunasamā yudhi |
yuyudhāno virāṭaśca drupadaśca mahārathaḥ
verses.meaning: Here are heroes, great archers, the equals of Bhima and Arjuna in battle: Yuyudhana, Virata, and Drupada the great warrior.
verses.takeaway: Know the strengths across the field.

verses.devanagari:
धृष्टकेतुश्चेकितानः काशिराजश्च वीर्यवान् ।
पुरुजित्कुन्तिभोजश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुङ्गवः
verses.iast:
dhṛṣṭaketuścekitānaḥ kāśirājaśca vīryavān |
purujitkuntibhojaśca śaibyaśca narapuṅgavaḥ
verses.meaning: Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana, the brave king of Kashi, Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaibya, the best of men.
verses.takeaway: Count carefully before you conclude.

verses.devanagari:
युधामन्युश्च विक्रान्त उत्तमौजाश्च वीर्यवान् ।
सौभद्रो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्व एव महारथाः
verses.iast:
yudhāmanyuśca vikrānta uttamaujāśca vīryavān |
saubhadro draupadeyāśca sarva eva mahārathāḥ
verses.meaning: Yudhamanyu and the strong Uttamaujas, Abhimanyu, and Draupadi's sons — all of them great warriors.
verses.takeaway: Finish the count before you judge.

verses.devanagari:
अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम ।
नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते
verses.iast:
asmākaṃ tu viśiṣṭā ye tānnibodha dvijottama |
nāyakā mama sainyasya saṃjñārthaṃ tānbravīmi te
verses.meaning: Now hear about our own chiefs, O best of learned men. I will name the leaders of my army so you know them.
verses.takeaway: Know your own team as well as the other side.

verses.devanagari:
भवान्भीष्मश्च कर्णश्च कृपश्च समितिंजयः ।
अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च सौमदत्तिस्तथैव च
verses.iast:
bhavānbhīṣmaśca karṇaśca kṛpaśca samitiṃjayaḥ |
aśvatthāmā vikarṇaśca saumadattistathaiva ca
verses.meaning: Yourself, and Bhishma, Karna, Kripa the winner of battles, Ashvatthama, Vikarna, and Somadatta's son.
verses.takeaway: Name the pillars that hold you up.

verses.devanagari:
अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः ।
नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः
verses.iast:
anye ca bahavaḥ śūrā madarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ |
nānāśastrapraharaṇāḥ sarve yuddhaviśāradāḥ
verses.meaning: And many other heroes, skilled with every kind of weapon. They have given up their lives for me.
verses.takeaway: Loyalty itself is a kind of strength.

verses.devanagari:
अपर्याप्तं तदस्माकं बलं भीष्माभिरक्षितम् ।
पर्याप्तं त्विदमेतेषां बलं भीमाभिरक्षितम्
verses.iast:
aparyāptaṃ tadasmākaṃ balaṃ bhīṣmābhirakṣitam |
paryāptaṃ tvidameteṣāṃ balaṃ bhīmābhirakṣitam
verses.meaning: Our army, guarded by Bhishma, is beyond measure; theirs, guarded by Bhima, is small.
verses.takeaway: Notice how each leader counts strength in his own favor.

verses.devanagari:
अयनेषु च सर्वेषु यथाभागमवस्थिताः ।
भीष्ममेवाभिरक्षन्तु भवन्तः सर्व एव हि
verses.iast:
ayaneṣu ca sarveṣu yathābhāgamavasthitāḥ |
bhīṣmamevābhirakṣantu bhavantaḥ sarva eva hi
verses.meaning: So hold the positions given to you, all of you. And protect Bhishma above everything.
verses.takeaway: Guard whatever holds everything else together.

verses.devanagari:
तस्य संजनयन्हर्षं कुरुवृद्धः पितामहः ।
सिंहनादं विनद्योच्चैः शङ्खं दध्मौ प्रतापवान्
verses.iast:
tasya saṃjanayanharṣaṃ kuruvṛddhaḥ pitāmahaḥ |
siṃhanādaṃ vinadyoccaiḥ śaṅkhaṃ dadhmau pratāpavān
verses.meaning: To cheer Duryodhana up, old grandsire Bhishma roared like a lion and blew his conch.
verses.takeaway: A small signal can lift a whole side.

verses.devanagari:
ततः शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च पणवानकगोमुखाः ।
सहसैवाभ्यहन्यन्त स शब्दस्तुमुलोऽभवत्
verses.iast:
tataḥ śaṅkhāśca bheryaśca paṇavānakagomukhāḥ |
sahasaivābhyahanyanta sa śabdastumulo'bhavat
verses.meaning: Then all at once conches, drums, cymbals and horns sounded, and the noise was tremendous.
verses.takeaway: Momentum has a sound.

verses.devanagari:
ततः श्वेतैर्हयैर्युक्ते महति स्यन्दने स्थितौ ।
माधवः पाण्डवश्चैव दिव्यौ शङ्खौ प्रदध्मतुः
verses.iast:
tataḥ śvetairhayairyukte mahati syandane sthitau |
mādhavaḥ pāṇḍavaścaiva divyau śaṅkhau pradadhmatuḥ
verses.meaning: Then Krishna and Arjuna, standing in their grand chariot yoked with white horses, blew their divine conches.
verses.takeaway: Answer noise with presence.

verses.devanagari:
पाञ्चजन्यं हृषीकेशो देवदत्तं धनञ्जयः ।
पौण्ड्रं दध्मौ महाशङ्खं भीमकर्मा वृकोदरः
verses.iast:
pāñcajanyaṃ hṛṣīkeśo devadattaṃ dhanañjayaḥ |
pauṇḍraṃ dadhmau mahāśaṅkhaṃ bhīmakarmā vṛkodaraḥ
verses.meaning: Hrishikesha blew Panchajanya, Arjuna blew Devadatta, and fearsome Bhima blew the great Paundra.
verses.takeaway: In this army, even the instruments have names.

verses.devanagari:
अनन्तविजयं राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः ।
नकुलः सहदेवश्च सुघोषमणिपुष्पकौ
verses.iast:
anantavijayaṃ rājā kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ |
nakulaḥ sahadevaśca sughoṣamaṇipuṣpakau
verses.meaning: Yudhishthira blew Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva blew Sughosha and Manipushpaka.
verses.takeaway: Everyone sounds their part.

verses.devanagari:
काश्यश्च परमेष्वासः शिखण्डी च महारथः ।
धृष्टद्युम्नो विराटश्च सात्यकिश्चापराजितः
verses.iast:
kāśyaśca parameṣvāsaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca mahārathaḥ |
dhṛṣṭadyumno virāṭaśca sātyakiścāparājitaḥ
verses.meaning: The king of Kashi with his fine bow, Shikhandi, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, and the unbeaten Satyaki.
verses.takeaway: No one on that field is nameless.

verses.devanagari:
द्रुपदो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः पृथिवीपते ।
सौभद्रश्च महाबाहुः शङ्खान्दध्मुः पृथक्पृथक्
verses.iast:
drupado draupadeyāśca sarvaśaḥ pṛthivīpate |
saubhadraśca mahābāhuḥ śaṅkhāndadhmuḥ pṛthakpṛthak
verses.meaning: Drupada, Draupadi's sons, and mighty-armed Abhimanyu blew their conches, each apart.
verses.takeaway: Each voice joins in turn.

verses.devanagari:
स घोषो धार्तराष्ट्राणां हृदयानि व्यदारयत् ।
नभश्च पृथिवीं चैव तुमुलो व्यनुनादयन्
verses.iast:
sa ghoṣo dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ hṛdayāni vyadārayat |
nabhaśca pṛthivīṃ caiva tumulo vyanunādayan
verses.meaning: That din tore the hearts of Dhritarashtra's men, echoing through the sky and the earth.
verses.takeaway: Sound alone can shake an army.

verses.devanagari:
अथ व्यवस्थितान्दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान्कपिध्वजः ।
प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसंपाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः
verses.iast:
atha vyavasthitāndṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrānkapidhvajaḥ |
pravṛtte śastrasaṃpāte dhanurudyamya pāṇḍavaḥ
verses.meaning: Then Arjuna, whose banner bears Hanuman, raised his bow as the weapons began to fly.
verses.takeaway: When the moment comes, positions get taken.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन
verses.devanagari:
हृषीकेशं तदा वाक्यमिदमाह महीपते ।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये रथं स्थापय मेऽच्युत
verses.iast:
hṛṣīkeśaṃ tadā vākyamidamāha mahīpate |
senayorubhayormadhye rathaṃ sthāpaya me'cyuta
verses.meaning: Arjuna addressed these words to Krishna.
verses.takeaway: Ask clearly for what you need.

verses.devanagari:
यावदेतान्निरिक्षेऽहं योद्‌धुकामानवस्थितान् ।
कैर्मया सह योद्धव्यमस्मिन् रणसमुद्यमे
verses.iast:
yāvadetānnirikṣe'haṃ yod‌dhukāmānavasthitān |
kairmayā saha yoddhavyamasmin raṇasamudyame
verses.meaning: O faultless Krishna, drive my chariot between the two armies. Let me see who stands here eager to fight, and with whom I must do battle.
verses.takeaway: Look first. Fight later — if at all.

verses.devanagari:
योत्स्यमानानवेक्षेऽहं य एतेऽत्र समागताः ।
धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्युद्धे प्रियचिकीर्षवः
verses.iast:
yotsyamānānavekṣe'haṃ ya ete'tra samāgatāḥ |
dhārtarāṣṭrasya durbuddheryuddhe priyacikīrṣavaḥ
verses.meaning: I will observe all those gathered here to fight, wishing to serve Duryodhana, the ill-minded son of Dhritarashtra, in battle.
verses.takeaway: Name why everyone is here — even the uncomfortable parts.

verses.speaker: सञ्जय
verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्तो हृषीकेशो गुडाकेशेन भारत ।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये स्थापयित्वा रथोत्तमम्
verses.iast:
evamukto hṛṣīkeśo guḍākeśena bhārata |
senayorubhayormadhye sthāpayitvā rathottamam
verses.meaning: Sanjaya said: so addressed by Arjuna, conqueror of sleep, Krishna stationed the splendid chariot between the two armies. It faced Bhishma.
verses.takeaway: A good friend does what you ask, no questions yet.

verses.devanagari:
भीष्मद्रोणप्रमुखतः सर्वेषां च महीक्षिताम् ।
उवाच पार्थ पश्यैतान्समवेतान्कुरूनिति
verses.iast:
bhīṣmadroṇapramukhataḥ sarveṣāṃ ca mahīkṣitām |
uvāca pārtha paśyaitānsamavetānkurūniti
verses.meaning: And before Bhishma, Drona and all the kings of the earth, Krishna said: O Arjuna, behold these Kurus gathered together.
verses.takeaway: Sometimes you have to look, even when it hurts.

verses.devanagari:
तत्रापश्यत्स्थितान्पार्थः पितॄनथ पितामहान् ।
आचार्यान्मातुलान्भ्रातॄन्पुत्रान्पौत्रान्सखींस्तथा
verses.iast:
tatrāpaśyatsthitānpārthaḥ pitṝnatha pitāmahān |
ācāryānmātulānbhrātṝnputrānpautrānsakhīṃstathā
verses.meaning: There Arjuna saw fathers and grandfathers. Teachers, uncles, brothers, sons and grandsons — and comrades.
verses.takeaway: The enemy has faces you know.

verses.devanagari:
श्वशुरान्सुहृदश्चैव सेनयोरुभयोरपि ।
तान्समीक्ष्य स कौन्तेयः सर्वान्बन्धूनवस्थितान्
verses.iast:
śvaśurānsuhṛdaścaiva senayorubhayorapi |
tānsamīkṣya sa kaunteyaḥ sarvānbandhūnavasthitān
verses.meaning: Arjuna saw fathers-in-law and friends on both sides — all his kin arrayed for war. Pity overwhelmed him, and he spoke in despair.
verses.takeaway: Strength that cannot feel is just armor.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन
verses.devanagari:
कृपया परयाविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत् ।
दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम्
verses.iast:
kṛpayā parayāviṣṭo viṣīdannidamabravīt |
dṛṣṭvemaṃ svajanaṃ kṛṣṇa yuyutsuṃ samupasthitam
verses.meaning: Arjuna said: seeing these kinsmen come to fight, Krishna, my limbs fail me and my mouth goes dry.
verses.takeaway: The body speaks before the mind catches up.

verses.devanagari:
सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति ।
वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते
verses.iast:
sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhaṃ ca pariśuṣyati |
vepathuśca śarīre me romaharṣaśca jāyate
verses.meaning: My body trembles and my hair stands on end.
verses.takeaway: Fear has a physiology.

verses.devanagari:
गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते ।
न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः
verses.iast:
gāṇḍīvaṃ sraṃsate hastāttvakcaiva paridahyate |
na ca śaknomyavasthātuṃ bhramatīva ca me manaḥ
verses.meaning: My great bow slips from my hand, my skin burns, and I cannot even stand steady.
verses.takeaway: Collapse is data, not disgrace.

verses.devanagari:
निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव ।
न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे
verses.iast:
nimittāni ca paśyāmi viparītāni keśava |
na ca śreyo'nupaśyāmi hatvā svajanamāhave
verses.meaning: My mind reels as if drunk. I see bad omens, Krishna, and no good at all in killing my own kin.
verses.takeaway: When the mind spins, name exactly what you see.

verses.devanagari:
न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च ।
किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा
verses.iast:
na kāṅkṣe vijayaṃ kṛṣṇa na ca rājyaṃ sukhāni ca |
kiṃ no rājyena govinda kiṃ bhogairjīvitena vā
verses.meaning: I want no victory, Krishna, no kingdom, no pleasures.
verses.takeaway: Ask what the prize is actually worth.

verses.devanagari:
येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च ।
त इमेऽवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च
verses.iast:
yeṣāmarthe kāṅkṣitaṃ no rājyaṃ bhogāḥ sukhāni ca |
ta ime'vasthitā yuddhe prāṇāṃstyaktvā dhanāni ca
verses.meaning: Of what use is a kingdom to us, Govinda? What use are pleasures, or even life?
verses.takeaway: Count the cost before you name the prize.

verses.devanagari:
आचार्याः पितरः पुत्रास्तथैव च पितामहाः ।
मातुलाः श्वशुराः पौत्राः श्यालाः संबन्धिनस्तथा
verses.iast:
ācāryāḥ pitaraḥ putrāstathaiva ca pitāmahāḥ |
mātulāḥ śvaśurāḥ pautrāḥ śyālāḥ saṃbandhinastathā
verses.meaning: The very people we want kingdoms and pleasures for stand here ready to die. Teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, uncles, in-laws, grandsons, brothers-in-law, kin.
verses.takeaway: Look at who pays for your win.

verses.devanagari:
एतान्न हन्तुमिच्छामि घ्नतोऽपि मधुसूदन ।
अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते
verses.iast:
etānna hantumicchāmi ghnato'pi madhusūdana |
api trailokyarājyasya hetoḥ kiṃ nu mahīkṛte
verses.meaning: I do not wish to kill these men, though they would kill me — not even to rule the three worlds, let alone this earth.
verses.takeaway: Some prices are too high at any scale.

verses.devanagari:
निहत्य धार्तराष्ट्रान्नः का प्रीतिः स्याज्जनार्दन ।
पापमेवाश्रयेदस्मान्हत्वैतानाततायिनः
verses.iast:
nihatya dhārtarāṣṭrānnaḥ kā prītiḥ syājjanārdana |
pāpamevāśrayedasmānhatvaitānātatāyinaḥ
verses.meaning: What joy would be ours, Janardana, after killing Dhritarashtra's sons? Killing these criminals, sin alone would cling to us.
verses.takeaway: A victory that costs your conscience isn't one.

verses.devanagari:
तस्मान्नार्हा वयं हन्तुं धार्तराष्ट्रान्स्वबान्धवान् ।
स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव
verses.iast:
tasmānnārhā vayaṃ hantuṃ dhārtarāṣṭrānsvabāndhavān |
svajanaṃ hi kathaṃ hatvā sukhinaḥ syāma mādhava
verses.meaning: So we must not kill our kinsmen. How could we ever be happy, Madhava, after killing our own people?
verses.takeaway: Ask the morning-after question before, not after.

verses.devanagari:
यद्यप्येते न पश्यन्ति लोभोपहतचेतसः ।
कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं मित्रद्रोहे च पातकम्
verses.iast:
yadyapyete na paśyanti lobhopahatacetasaḥ |
kulakṣayakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ mitradrohe ca pātakam
verses.meaning: Even though these men, blinded by greed, see no evil in wiping out a family or betraying friends —
verses.takeaway: Someone else's blindness doesn't excuse yours.

verses.devanagari:
कथं न ज्ञेयमस्माभिः पापादस्मान्निवर्तितुम् ।
कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं प्रपश्यद्भिर्जनार्दन
verses.iast:
kathaṃ na jñeyamasmābhiḥ pāpādasmānnivartitum |
kulakṣayakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ prapaśyadbhirjanārdana
verses.meaning: should not we, who DO see the evil in destroying a family, turn back from this sin?
verses.takeaway: Seeing clearly obligates you.

verses.devanagari:
कुलक्षये प्रणश्यन्ति कुलधर्माः सनातनाः ।
धर्मे नष्टे कुलं कृत्स्नमधर्मोऽभिभवत्युत
verses.iast:
kulakṣaye praṇaśyanti kuladharmāḥ sanātanāḥ |
dharme naṣṭe kulaṃ kṛtsnamadharmo'bhibhavatyuta
verses.meaning: When a family dies out, its timeless duties die with it. And when duty dies, lawlessness takes over the whole clan.
verses.takeaway: What holds people together needs tending, or it rots.

verses.devanagari:
अधर्माभिभवात्कृष्ण प्रदुष्यन्ति कुलस्त्रियः ।
स्त्रीषु दुष्टासु वार्ष्णेय जायते वर्णसंकरः
verses.iast:
adharmābhibhavātkṛṣṇa praduṣyanti kulastriyaḥ |
strīṣu duṣṭāsu vārṣṇeya jāyate varṇasaṃkaraḥ
verses.meaning: When lawlessness wins, Krishna, the women of the house go astray, and from that comes the mixing of duties.
verses.takeaway: He traces one crack as it spreads through the whole wall.

verses.devanagari:
संकरो नरकायैव कुलघ्नानां कुलस्य च ।
पतन्ति पितरो ह्येषां लुप्तपिण्डोदकक्रियाः
verses.iast:
saṃkaro narakāyaiva kulaghnānāṃ kulasya ca |
patanti pitaro hyeṣāṃ luptapiṇḍodakakriyāḥ
verses.meaning: That mixing drags the family and its destroyers down to hell. The forefathers fall, their offerings of food and water cut off.
verses.takeaway: Actions outlive their moment.

verses.devanagari:
दोषैरेतैः कुलघ्नानां वर्णसंकरकारकैः ।
उत्साद्यन्ते जातिधर्माः कुलधर्माश्च शाश्वताः
verses.iast:
doṣairetaiḥ kulaghnānāṃ varṇasaṃkarakārakaiḥ |
utsādyante jātidharmāḥ kuladharmāśca śāśvatāḥ
verses.meaning: The destroyers' misdeeds wipe out the timeless duties of ranks and families.
verses.takeaway: Small breaks compound.

verses.devanagari:
उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणां मनुष्याणां जनार्दन ।
नरकेऽनियतं वासो भवतीत्यनुशुश्रुम
verses.iast:
utsannakuladharmāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ janārdana |
narake'niyataṃ vāso bhavatītyanuśuśruma
verses.meaning: And we have heard, Janardana, that men without family duties must live in hell.
verses.takeaway: Tradition is cited as witness, not proof — note the honesty in 'we have heard.'

verses.devanagari:
अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम् ।
यद्राज्यसुखलोभेन हन्तुं स्वजनमुद्यताः
verses.iast:
aho bata mahatpāpaṃ kartuṃ vyavasitā vayam |
yadrājyasukhalobhena hantuṃ svajanamudyatāḥ
verses.meaning: Alas! We are set to commit a terrible sin, ready to kill our own kin out of greed for a kingdom's pleasures.
verses.takeaway: Naming it plainly is the first honest act.

verses.devanagari:
यदि मामप्रतीकारमशस्त्रं शस्त्रपाणयः ।
धार्तराष्ट्रा रणे हन्युस्तन्मे क्षेमतरं भवेत्
verses.iast:
yadi māmapratīkāramaśastraṃ śastrapāṇayaḥ |
dhārtarāṣṭrā raṇe hanyustanme kṣemataraṃ bhavet
verses.meaning: If Dhritarashtra's sons killed me in battle — weaponless, refusing to fight back — that would be better for me.
verses.takeaway: He would rather die clean than win dirty.

verses.speaker: सञ्जय
verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्त्वार्जुनः संख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् ।
विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः
verses.iast:
evamuktvārjunaḥ saṃkhye rathopastha upāviśat |
visṛjya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ śokasaṃvignamānasaḥ
verses.meaning: Sanjaya said: having spoken thus, Arjuna dropped his bow and arrows. He sank into his chariot, his mind drowned in grief.
verses.takeaway: Sometimes the bravest move is putting the weapon down.

verses.speaker: सञ्जय
verses.devanagari:
तं तथा कृपयाविष्टमश्रुपूर्णाकुलेक्षणम् ।
विषीदन्तमिदं वाक्यमुवाच मधुसूदनः
verses.iast:
taṃ tathā kṛpayāviṣṭamaśrupūrṇākulekṣaṇam |
viṣīdantamidaṃ vākyamuvāca madhusūdanaḥ
verses.meaning: Sanjaya said: to Arjuna, drowned in pity, his eyes full of tears and troubled, Krishna spoke these words.
verses.takeaway: Help arrives when grief is deepest.

verses.devanagari:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
कुतस्त्वा कश्मलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम् ।
अनार्यजुष्टमस्वर्ग्यमकीर्तिकरमर्जुन
verses.iast:
śrībhagavānuvāca
kutastvā kaśmalamidaṃ viṣame samupasthitam |
anāryajuṣṭamasvargyamakīrtikaramarjuna
verses.meaning: Krishna said: where has this weakness come from, Arjuna, here on the field of battle? It suits no noble man, wins no heaven, and brings only shame.
verses.takeaway: Name weakness plainly before fighting it.

verses.devanagari:
क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते ।
क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप
verses.iast:
klaibyaṃ mā sma gamaḥ pārtha naitattvayyupapadyate |
kṣudraṃ hṛdayadaurbalyaṃ tyaktvottiṣṭha parantapa
verses.meaning: Do not turn coward, Arjuna. It does not suit you. Shake off this petty faint-heartedness and stand up, scorcher of foes.
verses.takeaway: You are bigger than this moment.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन
verses.devanagari:
कथं भीष्ममहं संख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन ।
इषुभिः प्रति योत्स्यामि पूजार्हावरिसूदन
verses.iast:
kathaṃ bhīṣmamahaṃ saṃkhye droṇaṃ ca madhusūdana |
iṣubhiḥ prati yotsyāmi pūjārhāvarisūdana
verses.meaning: Arjuna said: how can I shoot arrows at Bhishma and Drona in battle, Krishna? Both deserve my worship, destroyer of foes.
verses.takeaway: The hardest fights are against people you respect.

verses.devanagari:
गुरूनहत्वा हि महानुभावान् श्रेयो भोक्तुं भैक्ष्यमपीह लोके ।
हत्वार्थकामांस्तु गुरूनिहैव भुञ्जीय भोगान् रुधिरप्रदिग्धान्
verses.iast:
gurūnahatvā hi mahānubhāvān śreyo bhoktuṃ bhaikṣyamapīha loke |
hatvārthakāmāṃstu gurūnihaiva bhuñjīya bhogān rudhirapradigdhān
verses.meaning: Better to beg for food in this world than kill these great teachers. Killing them, I would enjoy only blood-stained pleasures.
verses.takeaway: Count what victory eats, not just what it feeds.

verses.devanagari:
न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयो यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः ।
यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषाम- स्तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः
verses.iast:
na caitadvidmaḥ kataranno garīyo yadvā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ |
yāneva hatvā na jijīviṣāma- ste'vasthitāḥ pramukhe dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ
verses.meaning: We do not even know which is better for us — victory or defeat. The sons of Dhritarashtra stand before us, and we would not want to live after killing them.
verses.takeaway: Uncertainty is honest; pretending otherwise is not.

verses.devanagari:
कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावः पृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसम्मूढचेताः ।
यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्चितं ब्रूहि तन्मे शिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम्
verses.iast:
kārpaṇyadoṣopahatasvabhāvaḥ pṛcchāmi tvāṃ dharmasammūḍhacetāḥ |
yacchreyaḥ syānniścitaṃ brūhi tanme śiṣyaste'haṃ śādhi māṃ tvāṃ prapannam
verses.meaning: My heart is poisoned by pity, and my mind is confused about duty. Tell me plainly what is good. I am your student now — teach me.
verses.takeaway: Asking for help is a decision, not a defeat.

verses.devanagari:
न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद् यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम् ।
अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धं राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम्
verses.iast:
na hi prapaśyāmi mamāpanudyād yacchokamucchoṣaṇamindriyāṇām |
avāpya bhūmāvasapatnamṛddhaṃ rājyaṃ surāṇāmapi cādhipatyam
verses.meaning: I see nothing that could drive away this grief. It dries up my senses. Not rule over a rich, unrivaled earth. Not even lordship of the gods.
verses.takeaway: Grief does not negotiate.

verses.speaker: सञ्जय
verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशः परन्तप ।
न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह
verses.iast:
evamuktvā hṛṣīkeśaṃ guḍākeśaḥ parantapa |
na yotsya iti govindamuktvā tūṣṇīṃ babhūva ha
verses.meaning: Sanjaya said: having spoken thus to Krishna, Arjuna said, I will not fight — and fell silent.
verses.takeaway: Sometimes the sentence ends with silence.

verses.devanagari:
तमुवाच हृषीकेशः प्रहसन्निव भारत ।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये विषीदन्तमिदं वचः
verses.iast:
tamuvāca hṛṣīkeśaḥ prahasanniva bhārata |
senayorubhayormadhye viṣīdantamidaṃ vacaḥ
verses.meaning: To Arjuna, grieving between the two armies, Krishna spoke these words with a slight smile.
verses.takeaway: A smile before hard truths.

verses.devanagari:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे ।
गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः
verses.iast:
śrībhagavānuvāca
aśocyānanvaśocastvaṃ prajñāvādāṃśca bhāṣase |
gatāsūnagatāsūṃśca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ
verses.meaning: You grieve for those who deserve no grief, yet your words sound wise. The wise grieve neither for the living nor for the dead.
verses.takeaway: Grief has a proper object. Find it.

verses.devanagari:
न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः ।
न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम्
verses.iast:
na tvevāhaṃ jātu nāsaṃ na tvaṃ neme janādhipāḥ |
na caiva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarve vayamataḥ param
verses.meaning: Never was there a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor these kings. And none of us will ever cease to be.
verses.takeaway: You are older than your birthday.

verses.devanagari:
देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा ।
तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति
verses.iast:
dehino'sminyathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā |
tathā dehāntaraprāptirdhīrastatra na muhyati
verses.meaning: As childhood, youth, and old age come to the body, so the self moves on to another body. Steady people are not confused by this.
verses.takeaway: Change of address, not end of story.

verses.devanagari:
मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः ।
आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत
verses.iast:
mātrāsparśāstu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ |
āgamāpāyino'nityāstāṃstitikṣasva bhārata
verses.meaning: Cold and heat, pleasure and pain come and go with the senses, Arjuna. They are not permanent — bear them.
verses.takeaway: Feelings are weather, not climate.

verses.devanagari:
यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ ।
समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते
verses.iast:
yaṃ hi na vyathayantyete puruṣaṃ puruṣarṣabha |
samaduḥkhasukhaṃ dhīraṃ so'mṛtatvāya kalpate
verses.meaning: The person these cannot shake — steady in pain and pleasure alike — is fit for deathlessness.
verses.takeaway: Steadiness is a superpower.

verses.devanagari:
नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः ।
उभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः
verses.iast:
nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ |
ubhayorapi dṛṣṭo'ntastvanayostattvadarśibhiḥ
verses.meaning: The unreal never truly is; the real never ceases to be. Those who see truth perceive both correctly.
verses.takeaway: Learn to tell the passing from the permanent.

verses.devanagari:
अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ।
विनाशमव्ययस्यास्य न कश्चित्कर्तुमर्हति
verses.iast:
avināśi tu tadviddhi yena sarvamidaṃ tatam |
vināśamavyayasyāsya na kaścitkartumarhati
verses.meaning: Know that which fills this whole world to be indestructible. No one can destroy the imperishable.
verses.takeaway: What is everywhere cannot be broken anywhere.

verses.devanagari:
अन्तवन्त इमे देहा नित्यस्योक्ताः शरीरिणः ।
अनाशिनोऽप्रमेयस्य तस्माद्युध्यस्व भारत
verses.iast:
antavanta ime dehā nityasyoktāḥ śarīriṇaḥ |
anāśino'prameyasya tasmādyudhyasva bhārata
verses.meaning: These bodies, belonging to the eternal, indestructible, immeasurable self, must come to an end. So fight, Arjuna.
verses.takeaway: The conclusion lands like a hammer — on purpose.

verses.devanagari:
य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम् ।
उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते
verses.iast:
ya enaṃ vetti hantāraṃ yaścainaṃ manyate hatam |
ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṃ hanti na hanyate
verses.meaning: Whoever thinks the self kills, and whoever thinks it is killed — both are wrong. It kills not, and is not killed.
verses.takeaway: The self is not the body. Sit with that.

verses.devanagari:
न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः ।
अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे
verses.iast:
na jāyate mriyate vā kadācinnāyaṃ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ |
ajo nityaḥ śāśvato'yaṃ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre
verses.meaning: It is never born and never dies. Unborn, eternal, ancient — it is not killed when the body is killed.
verses.takeaway: Older than old.

verses.devanagari:
वेदाविनाशिनं नित्यं य एनमजमव्ययम् ।
कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम्
verses.iast:
vedāvināśinaṃ nityaṃ ya enamajamavyayam |
kathaṃ sa puruṣaḥ pārtha kaṃ ghātayati hanti kam
verses.meaning: Know the self as indestructible, eternal, unborn, imperishable. Then ask: how could such a person kill — or cause killing?
verses.takeaway: Understanding changes what your hands can do.

verses.devanagari:
वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि ।
तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णान्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही
verses.iast:
vāsāṃsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya navāni gṛhṇāti naro'parāṇi |
tathā śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇānyanyāni saṃyāti navāni dehī
verses.meaning: A person drops worn-out clothes and puts on new ones. So the self drops worn-out bodies and enters new ones.
verses.takeaway: The most famous image in the book — and it earns it.

verses.devanagari:
नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः ।
न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः
verses.iast:
nainaṃ chindanti śastrāṇi nainaṃ dahati pāvakaḥ |
na cainaṃ kledayantyāpo na śoṣayati mārutaḥ
verses.meaning: Weapons cannot cut it, fire cannot burn it, water cannot wet it, wind cannot dry it.
verses.takeaway: List what cannot touch you. It is longer than you think.

verses.devanagari:
अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च ।
नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः
verses.iast:
acchedyo'yamadāhyo'yamakledyo'śoṣya eva ca |
nityaḥ sarvagataḥ sthāṇuracalo'yaṃ sanātanaḥ
verses.meaning: It cannot be cut or burned. Not wetted or dried. It is eternal, everywhere, steady, firm, everlasting.
verses.takeaway: Five adjectives for what does not change; zero for what does. Notice the ratio.

verses.devanagari:
अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्योऽयमुच्यते ।
तस्मादेवं विदित्वैनं नानुशोचितुमर्हसि
verses.iast:
avyakto'yamacintyo'yamavikāryo'yamucyate |
tasmādevaṃ viditvainaṃ nānuśocitumarhasi
verses.meaning: It is called unperceived, unthinkable, unchanging. Knowing the self as such, you should not grieve.
verses.takeaway: Some things are understood by admitting they cannot be pictured.

verses.devanagari:
अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम् ।
तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैवं शोचितुमर्हसि
verses.iast:
atha cainaṃ nityajātaṃ nityaṃ vā manyase mṛtam |
tathāpi tvaṃ mahābāho naivaṃ śocitumarhasi
verses.meaning: But even if you think the self is constantly born and constantly dying — even then, you should not grieve.
verses.takeaway: Krishna argues the other side too. Steelman everything.

verses.devanagari:
जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च ।
तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि
verses.iast:
jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyurdhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca |
tasmādaparihārye'rthe na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi
verses.meaning: For to one that is born, death is certain; and to one that dies, birth is certain. So for what cannot be avoided, you should not grieve.
verses.takeaway: Grief over the inevitable is optional suffering.

verses.devanagari:
अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत ।
अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना
verses.iast:
avyaktādīni bhūtāni vyaktamadhyāni bhārata |
avyaktanidhanānyeva tatra kā paridevanā
verses.meaning: All beings begin unseen, appear in the middle, and end unseen. What is there to mourn in that?
verses.takeaway: The visible part was always the middle.

verses.devanagari:
आश्चर्यवत्पश्यति कश्चिदेनमाश्चर्यवद्वदति तथैव चान्यः ।
आश्चर्यवच्चैनमन्यः शृणोति श्रुत्वाप्येनं वेद न चैव कश्चित्
verses.iast:
āścaryavatpaśyati kaścidenamāścaryavadvadati tathaiva cānyaḥ |
āścaryavaccainamanyaḥ śṛṇoti śrutvāpyenaṃ veda na caiva kaścit
verses.meaning: One person sees the self as a wonder. Another speaks of it as a wonder. A third hears of it as a wonder. And even hearing it, no one truly knows it.
verses.takeaway: The deepest things stay strange. That is fine.

verses.devanagari:
देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्वस्य भारत ।
तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि
verses.iast:
dehī nityamavadhyo'yaṃ dehe sarvasya bhārata |
tasmātsarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi
verses.meaning: The self dwelling in every body can never be killed. So grieve for no being.
verses.takeaway: The argument closes where it opened — with grief itself.

verses.devanagari:
स्वधर्ममपि चावेक्ष्य न विकम्पितुमर्हसि ।
धर्म्याद्धि युद्धाच्छ्रेयोऽन्यत्क्षत्रियस्य न विद्यते
verses.iast:
svadharmamapi cāvekṣya na vikampitumarhasi |
dharmyāddhi yuddhācchreyo'nyatkṣatriyasya na vidyate
verses.meaning: Looking to your own duty as well, you must not waver. For a warrior, nothing is better than a righteous battle.
verses.takeaway: Duty is not passion — it is assignment.

verses.devanagari:
यदृच्छया चोपपन्नं स्वर्गद्वारमपावृतम् ।
सुखिनः क्षत्रियाः पार्थ लभन्ते युद्धमीदृशम्
verses.iast:
yadṛcchayā copapannaṃ svargadvāramapāvṛtam |
sukhinaḥ kṣatriyāḥ pārtha labhante yuddhamīdṛśam
verses.meaning: Happy are the warriors who find such a battle come of itself — an open door to heaven.
verses.takeaway: Rare chances are doors. Walk through.

verses.devanagari:
अथ चेत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं संग्रामं न करिष्यसि ।
ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि
verses.iast:
atha cettvamimaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ na kariṣyasi |
tataḥ svadharmaṃ kīrtiṃ ca hitvā pāpamavāpsyasi
verses.meaning: But if you refuse this righteous battle, you abandon duty and honor — and take on sin.
verses.takeaway: Refusal is also a choice, with its own bill.

verses.devanagari:
अकीर्तिं चापि भूतानि कथयिष्यन्ति तेऽव्ययाम् ।
सम्भावितस्य चाकीर्तिर्मरणादतिरिच्यते
verses.iast:
akīrtiṃ cāpi bhūtāni kathayiṣyanti te'vyayām |
sambhāvitasya cākīrtirmaraṇādatiricyate
verses.meaning: All beings will tell of your lasting shame. And for an honored person, shame is worse than death.
verses.takeaway: Reputation is currency. Spend it knowingly.

verses.devanagari:
भयाद्रणादुपरतं मंस्यन्ते त्वां महारथाः ।
येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम्
verses.iast:
bhayādraṇāduparataṃ maṃsyante tvāṃ mahārathāḥ |
yeṣāṃ ca tvaṃ bahumato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam
verses.meaning: The great warriors will think you fled from fear. Fallen from their esteem, you will sink low.
verses.takeaway: Cowardice has compound interest.

verses.devanagari:
अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून्वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः ।
निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम्
verses.iast:
avācyavādāṃśca bahūnvadiṣyanti tavāhitāḥ |
nindantastava sāmarthyaṃ tato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim
verses.meaning: Your enemies will mock your strength with cruel words. What could hurt more than that?
verses.takeaway: He counts the cost of walking away, rupee by rupee.

verses.devanagari:
हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम् ।
तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः
verses.iast:
hato vā prāpsyasi svargaṃ jitvā vā bhokṣyase mahīm |
tasmāduttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛtaniścayaḥ
verses.meaning: Killed, you win heaven; victorious, you enjoy the earth. So rise up, determined to fight.
verses.takeaway: Both outcomes honored. Only standing still is shameful.

verses.devanagari:
सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ ।
ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि
verses.iast:
sukhaduḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau |
tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṃ pāpamavāpsyasi
verses.meaning: Treating pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat as the same, fight — and you will incur no sin.
verses.takeaway: The equation that runs the whole book.

verses.devanagari:
एषा तेऽभिहिता सांख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां शृणु ।
बुद्ध्या युक्तो यया पार्थ कर्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसि
verses.iast:
eṣā te'bhihitā sāṃkhye buddhiryoge tvimāṃ śṛṇu |
buddhyā yukto yayā pārtha karmabandhaṃ prahāsyasi
verses.meaning: This wisdom of understanding has been taught to you. Now hear the wisdom of discipline — holding it, you will break the bonds of action.
verses.takeaway: Two paths, one destination.

verses.devanagari:
नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते ।
स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात्
verses.iast:
nehābhikramanāśo'sti pratyavāyo na vidyate |
svalpamapyasya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt
verses.meaning: On this path no effort is wasted and no obstacle exists. Even a little of this discipline saves you from great fear.
verses.takeaway: Small steps count in full.

verses.devanagari:
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन ।
बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम्
verses.iast:
vyavasāyātmikā buddhirekeha kurunandana |
bahuśākhā hyanantāśca buddhayo'vyavasāyinām
verses.meaning: Here there is one firm resolve. The thoughts of the irresolute branch endlessly.
verses.takeaway: One pointed mind beats a hundred clever ones.

verses.devanagari:
यामिमां पुष्पितां वाचं प्रवदन्त्यविपश्चितः ।
वेदवादरताः पार्थ नान्यदस्तीति वादिनः
verses.iast:
yāmimāṃ puṣpitāṃ vācaṃ pravadantyavipaścitaḥ |
vedavādaratāḥ pārtha nānyadastīti vādinaḥ
verses.meaning: The unwise love flowery Vedic phrases. They promise heaven and declare nothing else exists.
verses.takeaway: Beware beautiful words that end thinking.

verses.devanagari:
कामात्मानः स्वर्गपरा जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम् ।
क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति
verses.iast:
kāmātmānaḥ svargaparā janmakarmaphalapradām |
kriyāviśeṣabahulāṃ bhogaiśvaryagatiṃ prati
verses.meaning: Full of desires, heaven-bent, promising rebirth as the fruit of rites.
verses.takeaway: Wanting heaven can be its own trap.

verses.devanagari:
भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम् ।
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते
verses.iast:
bhogaiśvaryaprasaktānāṃ tayāpahṛtacetasām |
vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate
verses.meaning: Attached to pleasures and power, their minds stolen by such talk — they never reach steady resolve.
verses.takeaway: Wanting everything is how you hold nothing.

verses.devanagari:
त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन ।
निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान्
verses.iast:
traiguṇyaviṣayā vedā nistraiguṇyo bhavārjuna |
nirdvandvo nityasattvastho niryogakṣema ātmavān
verses.meaning: The Vedas deal with nature's three qualities. Rise above them, Arjuna — beyond opposites, steady, self-possessed.
verses.takeaway: Transcend the categories; do not redecorate them.

verses.devanagari:
यावानर्थ उदपाने सर्वतः संप्लुतोदके ।
तावान्सर्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः
verses.iast:
yāvānartha udapāne sarvataḥ saṃplutodake |
tāvānsarveṣu vedeṣu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ
verses.meaning: To the knower, all the Vedas are as useful as a water tank in a flooded land.
verses.takeaway: Outgrow the map once you have seen the territory.

verses.devanagari:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन ।
मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि
verses.iast:
karmaṇyevādhikāraste mā phaleṣu kadācana |
mā karmaphalaheturbhūrmā te saṅgo'stvakarmaṇi
verses.meaning: Your right is to action alone, never to its fruits. Never let results be your motive — and never sit idle either.
verses.takeaway: THE verse. Act fully, clutch nothing.

verses.devanagari:
योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनंजय ।
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते
verses.iast:
yogasthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā dhanaṃjaya |
siddhyasiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṃ yoga ucyate
verses.meaning: Established in discipline, do your work, dropping attachment. Steadiness in success and failure — that steadiness is discipline.
verses.takeaway: Discipline, defined in one line.

verses.devanagari:
दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनंजय ।
बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः
verses.iast:
dūreṇa hyavaraṃ karma buddhiyogāddhanaṃjaya |
buddhau śaraṇamanviccha kṛpaṇāḥ phalahetavaḥ
verses.meaning: Action done for gain sits far below the discipline of understanding. Take shelter in understanding. The profit-hunters are pitiful.
verses.takeaway: Work for wages, or work for wisdom. Know which.

verses.devanagari:
बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते ।
तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम्
verses.iast:
buddhiyukto jahātīha ubhe sukṛtaduṣkṛte |
tasmādyogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam
verses.meaning: Joined to understanding, one drops both good and bad deeds here. So devote yourself to discipline — skill in action is discipline.
verses.takeaway: Skill plus detachment. That is the whole formula.

verses.devanagari:
कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः ।
जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम्
verses.iast:
karmajaṃ buddhiyuktā hi phalaṃ tyaktvā manīṣiṇaḥ |
janmabandhavinirmuktāḥ padaṃ gacchantyanāmayam
verses.meaning: The wise join themselves to understanding. They drop the fruits of action. They walk free of rebirth's chains, to the place beyond sorrow.
verses.takeaway: The destination has a name: beyond sorrow.

verses.devanagari:
यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति ।
तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च
verses.iast:
yadā te mohakalilaṃ buddhirvyatitariṣyati |
tadā gantāsi nirvedaṃ śrotavyasya śrutasya ca
verses.meaning: When your understanding crosses past confusion, you will turn indifferent. Indifferent to everything heard — or yet to be heard.
verses.takeaway: Outgrow even the scriptures — it says so itself.

verses.devanagari:
श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला ।
समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि
verses.iast:
śrutivipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niścalā |
samādhāvacalā buddhistadā yogamavāpsyasi
verses.meaning: Your understanding is confused by hearsay today. When it stands firm and steady in contemplation, you will reach discipline.
verses.takeaway: Hold still long enough and stillness holds you.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन
verses.devanagari:
स्थितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्थस्य केशव ।
स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम्
verses.iast:
sthitaprajñasya kā bhāṣā samādhisthasya keśava |
sthitadhīḥ kiṃ prabhāṣeta kimāsīta vrajeta kim
verses.meaning: Arjuna said: what marks the steady-minded, Krishna? How does such a one speak, sit, walk?
verses.takeaway: The student asks the practical question.

verses.devanagari:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
प्रजहाति यदा कामान्सर्वान्पार्थ मनोगतान् ।
आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते
verses.iast:
śrībhagavānuvāca
prajahāti yadā kāmānsarvānpārtha manogatān |
ātmanyevātmanā tuṣṭaḥ sthitaprajñastadocyate
verses.meaning: When one drops all the mind's desires and rests content in the self, by the self — that one is called steady.
verses.takeaway: Want nothing, have everything.

verses.devanagari:
दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः ।
वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते
verses.iast:
duḥkheṣvanudvignamanāḥ sukheṣu vigataspṛhaḥ |
vītarāgabhayakrodhaḥ sthitadhīrmunirucyate
verses.meaning: Unshaken in sorrow. Uninterested in pleasures. Free of craving, fear, and anger. Such a sage is steady.
verses.takeaway: Steadiness has four enemies. Name yours.

verses.devanagari:
यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम् ।
नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता
verses.iast:
yaḥ sarvatrānabhisnehastattatprāpya śubhāśubham |
nābhinandati na dveṣṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
verses.meaning: Untied everywhere. Neither thrilled by good fortune nor disgusted by bad. Such understanding is steady.
verses.takeaway: Equanimity is not indifference. It is freedom.

verses.devanagari:
यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः ।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता
verses.iast:
yadā saṃharate cāyaṃ kūrmo'ṅgānīva sarvaśaḥ |
indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyastasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
verses.meaning: When one pulls the senses back from their objects, as a tortoise pulls in its limbs — understanding holds steady.
verses.takeaway: The tortoise is the book's favorite yogi.

verses.devanagari:
विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः ।
रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते
verses.iast:
viṣayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ |
rasavarjaṃ raso'pyasya paraṃ dṛṣṭvā nivartate
verses.meaning: Sense objects fade for the abstinent — but the taste lingers. Even taste leaves once the highest is seen.
verses.takeaway: Willpower starves; vision cures.

verses.devanagari:
यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः ।
इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः
verses.iast:
yatato hyapi kaunteya puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ |
indriyāṇi pramāthīni haranti prasabhaṃ manaḥ
verses.meaning: The senses are turbulent. They violently carry off the mind — even of a striving wise man.
verses.takeaway: Respect the opponent.

verses.devanagari:
तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः ।
वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता
verses.iast:
tāni sarvāṇi saṃyamya yukta āsīta matparaḥ |
vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
verses.meaning: Holding them all in check, sit devoted, with Me as the highest goal. Who masters the senses owns a steady mind.
verses.takeaway: Devotion here is a technique, not a sentiment.

verses.devanagari:
ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते ।
सङ्गात्संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते
verses.iast:
dhyāyato viṣayānpuṃsaḥ saṅgasteṣūpajāyate |
saṅgātsaṃjāyate kāmaḥ kāmātkrodho'bhijāyate
verses.meaning: Dwelling on sense objects breeds attachment. From attachment comes desire. From desire, anger.
verses.takeaway: The chain reaction, link by link.

verses.devanagari:
क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः ।
स्मृतिभ्रंशाद्बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति
verses.iast:
krodhādbhavati saṃmohaḥ saṃmohātsmṛtivibhramaḥ |
smṛtibhraṃśādbuddhināśo buddhināśātpraṇaśyati
verses.meaning: From anger comes confusion. From confusion, memory fails. With reason gone, one is destroyed.
verses.takeaway: Read it backwards as an escape manual.

verses.devanagari:
रागद्वेषवियुक्तैस्तु विषयानिन्द्रियैश्चरन् ।
आत्मवश्यैर्विधेयात्मा प्रसादमधिगच्छति
verses.iast:
rāgadveṣaviyuktaistu viṣayānindriyaiścaran |
ātmavaśyairvidheyātmā prasādamadhigacchati
verses.meaning: But one who moves among sense objects with senses ruled by the self will find peace. Free of likes and dislikes.
verses.takeaway: Not escape from the world. Mastery inside it.

verses.devanagari:
प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते ।
प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते
verses.iast:
prasāde sarvaduḥkhānāṃ hānirasyopajāyate |
prasannacetaso hyāśu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate
verses.meaning: In peace, all sorrows end; and the peaceful mind soon grows steady.
verses.takeaway: Peace first, steadiness follows. Not the reverse.

verses.devanagari:
नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना ।
न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम्
verses.iast:
nāsti buddhirayuktasya na cāyuktasya bhāvanā |
na cābhāvayataḥ śāntiraśāntasya kutaḥ sukham
verses.meaning: Without self-rule there is no understanding, no contemplation — and without contemplation, where is peace? Without peace, where is happiness?
verses.takeaway: Four rungs. Miss one, miss all.

verses.devanagari:
इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनु विधीयते ।
तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि
verses.iast:
indriyāṇāṃ hi caratāṃ yanmano'nu vidhīyate |
tadasya harati prajñāṃ vāyurnāvamivāmbhasi
verses.meaning: The mind that chases wandering senses loses judgment. As wind carries a boat on water.
verses.takeaway: Guard the helm.

verses.devanagari:
तस्माद्यस्य महाबाहो निगृहीतानि सर्वशः ।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता
verses.iast:
tasmādyasya mahābāho nigṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ |
indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyastasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
verses.meaning: So, mighty-armed one: hold the senses back from objects on every side. Then understanding stands firm.
verses.takeaway: The argument returns to fortify its own walls.

verses.devanagari:
या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी ।
यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः
verses.iast:
yā niśā sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī |
yasyāṃ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ
verses.meaning: What is night for all beings is day for the self-controlled; what is day for beings is night for the seer.
verses.takeaway: The awake and the asleep have swapped places.

verses.devanagari:
आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत् ।
तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी
verses.iast:
āpūryamāṇamacalapratiṣṭhaṃ samudramāpaḥ praviśanti yadvat |
tadvatkāmā yaṃ praviśanti sarve sa śāntimāpnoti na kāmakāmī
verses.meaning: Waters enter the full, unmoving ocean. So desires enter the sage. He finds peace — not the desirer.
verses.takeaway: Be the ocean, not the river.

verses.devanagari:
विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान् पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः ।
निर्ममो निरहंकारः स शान्तिमधिगच्छति
verses.iast:
vihāya kāmānyaḥ sarvān pumāṃścarati niḥspṛhaḥ |
nirmamo nirahaṃkāraḥ sa śāntimadhigacchati
verses.meaning: Dropping all desires, living free of mine-ness, ego and pride — such a one finds peace.
verses.takeaway: Four things to drop. Count them on one hand.

verses.devanagari:
एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति ।
स्थित्वास्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति
verses.iast:
eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṃ prāpya vimuhyati |
sthitvāsyāmantakāle'pi brahmanirvāṇamṛcchati
verses.meaning: This is the state of oneness with ultimate reality. Reaching it, one is never confused; settled in it even at death, one merges into its peace.
verses.takeaway: The chapter lands where it began — beyond grief.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन
verses.devanagari:
ज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन ।
तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव
verses.iast:
jyāyasī cetkarmaṇaste matā buddhirjanārdana |
tatkiṃ karmaṇi ghore māṃ niyojayasi keśava
verses.meaning: Arjuna said: if calm understanding is better than action, Krishna, why do you push me toward this terrible deed?
verses.takeaway: When advice confuses you, ask which part confused you.

verses.devanagari:
व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे ।
तदेकं वद निश्चित्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम्
verses.iast:
vyāmiśreṇeva vākyena buddhiṃ mohayasīva me |
tadekaṃ vada niścitya yena śreyo'hamāpnuyām
verses.meaning: Your words sound double-edged and confuse my mind. Tell me one clear thing by which I can reach the highest good.
verses.takeaway: Demand clarity. Confusion is data.

verses.devanagari:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
लोकेऽस्मिन्द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयानघ ।
ज्ञानयोगेन सांख्यानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम्
verses.iast:
śrībhagavānuvāca
loke'smindvividhā niṣṭhā purā proktā mayānagha |
jñānayogena sāṃkhyānāṃ karmayogena yoginām
verses.meaning: Krishna said: O faultless one, I have always taught two paths in this world. Understanding for the thinkers. Disciplined action for the doers.
verses.takeaway: Two doors, same house.

verses.devanagari:
न कर्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्यं पुरुषोऽश्नुते ।
न च संन्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति
verses.iast:
na karmaṇāmanārambhānnaiṣkarmyaṃ puruṣo'śnute |
na ca saṃnyasanādeva siddhiṃ samadhigacchati
verses.meaning: No one earns freedom from action by simply avoiding action. And no one reaches perfection by merely giving things up.
verses.takeaway: You cannot quit your way to freedom.

verses.devanagari:
न हि कश्चित्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत् ।
कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः
verses.iast:
na hi kaścitkṣaṇamapi jātu tiṣṭhatyakarmakṛt |
kāryate hyavaśaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛtijairguṇaiḥ
verses.meaning: No one can stay even a moment without acting. Nature forces everyone to act, like it or not.
verses.takeaway: Inaction is also an action. Choose accordingly.

verses.devanagari:
कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन् ।
इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते
verses.iast:
karmendriyāṇi saṃyamya ya āste manasā smaran |
indriyārthānvimūḍhātmā mithyācāraḥ sa ucyate
verses.meaning: Whoever locks down the senses but keeps dreaming of pleasures is a fraud — a hypocrite.
verses.takeaway: The performance of restraint is not restraint.

verses.devanagari:
यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन ।
कर्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते
verses.iast:
yastvindriyāṇi manasā niyamyārabhate'rjuna |
karmendriyaiḥ karmayogamasaktaḥ sa viśiṣyate
verses.meaning: But whoever steers the senses with the mind stands far above. Unattached. Body put to good work.
verses.takeaway: Control, don't amputate.

verses.devanagari:
नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः ।
शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः
verses.iast:
niyataṃ kuru karma tvaṃ karma jyāyo hyakarmaṇaḥ |
śarīrayātrāpi ca te na prasiddhyedakarmaṇaḥ
verses.meaning: So do your proper work. Action beats inaction — you cannot even keep your body going without it.
verses.takeaway: The basics first: eat, breathe, act.

verses.devanagari:
यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः ।
तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसङ्गः समाचर
verses.iast:
yajñārthātkarmaṇo'nyatra loko'yaṃ karmabandhanaḥ |
tadarthaṃ karma kaunteya muktasaṅgaḥ samācara
verses.meaning: This world is chained by every act except acts done as offering. So work as an offering, free of clinging.
verses.takeaway: Dedicate the work and the chains fall off.

verses.devanagari:
सहयज्ञाः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः ।
अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधुक्
verses.iast:
sahayajñāḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā purovāca prajāpatiḥ |
anena prasaviṣyadhvameṣa vo'stviṣṭakāmadhuk
verses.meaning: In the beginning the Creator made humans together with sacrifice, and said: grow with this. Let it grant everything you want.
verses.takeaway: The original deal: give, and it gives back.

verses.devanagari:
देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः ।
परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ
verses.iast:
devānbhāvayatānena te devā bhāvayantu vaḥ |
parasparaṃ bhāvayantaḥ śreyaḥ paramavāpsyatha
verses.meaning: Nourish the gods with sacrifice, and the gods will nourish you. Nourishing each other, you will reach the highest good.
verses.takeaway: Reciprocity runs the universe.

verses.devanagari:
इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः ।
तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः
verses.iast:
iṣṭānbhogānhi vo devā dāsyante yajñabhāvitāḥ |
tairdattānapradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ
verses.meaning: The gods give you the enjoyments you ask for. Whoever enjoys them without giving back is a thief.
verses.takeaway: Gratitude is the rent you pay for existence.

verses.devanagari:
यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः ।
भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात्
verses.iast:
yajñaśiṣṭāśinaḥ santo mucyante sarvakilbiṣaiḥ |
bhuñjate te tvaghaṃ pāpā ye pacantyātmakāraṇāt
verses.meaning: Good people who eat what remains after offering are freed from all wrong. The selfish, who cook only for themselves, eat sin.
verses.takeaway: Share first, eat second.

verses.devanagari:
अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः ।
यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः
verses.iast:
annādbhavanti bhūtāni parjanyādannasambhavaḥ |
yajñādbhavati parjanyo yajñaḥ karmasamudbhavaḥ
verses.meaning: From food come all creatures. From rain comes food. From sacrifice comes rain. And sacrifice comes from action.
verses.takeaway: Everything you are stands on a chain of giving.

verses.devanagari:
कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम् ।
तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम्
verses.iast:
karma brahmodbhavaṃ viddhi brahmākṣarasamudbhavam |
tasmātsarvagataṃ brahma nityaṃ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam
verses.meaning: Know that action comes from the Vedas, and the Vedas from the Imperishable. So the all-seeing Vedas forever turn around sacrifice.
verses.takeaway: Trace anything back far enough and you reach mystery.

verses.devanagari:
एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः ।
अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति
verses.iast:
evaṃ pravartitaṃ cakraṃ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ |
aghāyurindriyārāmo moghaṃ pārtha sa jīvati
verses.meaning: Whoever refuses to turn this wheel here — living in sin, slave to the senses — lives a wasted life.
verses.takeaway: Opt out of the cycle and you opt out of the point.

verses.devanagari:
यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः ।
आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते
verses.iast:
yastvātmaratireva syādātmatṛptaśca mānavaḥ |
ātmanyeva ca santuṣṭastasya kāryaṃ na vidyate
verses.meaning: But one who delights only in the self, content in the self, pleased with the self — has nothing left to do.
verses.takeaway: The exception that proves the whole teaching.

verses.devanagari:
नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन ।
न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्चिदर्थव्यपाश्रयः
verses.iast:
naiva tasya kṛtenārtho nākṛteneha kaścana |
na cāsya sarvabhūteṣu kaścidarthavyapāśrayaḥ
verses.meaning: Such a person gains nothing by acting and loses nothing by resting. And nobody's help does such a one need.
verses.takeaway: Need nothing, owe nothing. (Almost nobody lives here — yet.)

verses.devanagari:
तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर ।
असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः
verses.iast:
tasmādasaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara |
asakto hyācarankarma paramāpnoti pūruṣaḥ
verses.meaning: By action alone did Janaka and others reach perfection. Act — if only to hold the world together.
verses.takeaway: The masters worked. So should you.

verses.devanagari:
कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः ।
लोकसंग्रहमेवापि संपश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि
verses.iast:
karmaṇaiva hi saṃsiddhimāsthitā janakādayaḥ |
lokasaṃgrahamevāpi saṃpaśyankartumarhasi
verses.meaning: Whatever a great person does, others copy. People follow whatever such a one treats as right.
verses.takeaway: You are always being watched. Act like it.

verses.devanagari:
यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः ।
स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते
verses.iast:
yadyadācarati śreṣṭhastattadevetaro janaḥ |
sa yatpramāṇaṃ kurute lokastadanuvartate
verses.meaning: There is nothing I must do in all three worlds. Nothing to gain that I have not gained. And yet I keep working.
verses.takeaway: Even perfection shows up to work. What is your excuse?

verses.devanagari:
न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किंचन ।
नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि
verses.iast:
na me pārthāsti kartavyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu kiṃcana |
nānavāptamavāptavyaṃ varta eva ca karmaṇi
verses.meaning: For if I ever stopped working tirelessly, everyone would follow my path to ruin. If I abandoned action, these worlds would collapse, and I would destroy all beings.
verses.takeaway: The universe runs on someone showing up.

verses.devanagari:
यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः ।
मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः
verses.iast:
yadi hyahaṃ na varteyaṃ jātu karmaṇyatandritaḥ |
mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ
verses.meaning: If I stopped working, people would sink into laziness. Worlds would break. I would corrupt every race and ruin all beings.
verses.takeaway: Quitting has a blast radius.

verses.devanagari:
उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम् ।
संकरस्य च कर्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः
verses.iast:
utsīdeyurime lokā na kuryāṃ karma cedaham |
saṃkarasya ca kartā syāmupahanyāmimāḥ prajāḥ
verses.meaning: The ignorant act attached to their deeds. So should the wise act — unattached, to hold the world together.
verses.takeaway: Same actions, different grip.

verses.devanagari:
सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत ।
कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथासक्तश्चिकीर्षुर्लोकसंग्रहम्
verses.iast:
saktāḥ karmaṇyavidvāṃso yathā kurvanti bhārata |
kuryādvidvāṃstathāsaktaścikīrṣurlokasaṃgraham
verses.meaning: The wise should not shake the minds of the ignorant, who cling to deeds. Working devoutly themselves, let them set everyone to work.
verses.takeaway: Do not break beginners. Employ them.

verses.devanagari:
न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम् ।
जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान्युक्तः समाचरन्
verses.iast:
na buddhibhedaṃ janayedajñānāṃ karmasaṅginām |
joṣayetsarvakarmāṇi vidvānyuktaḥ samācaran
verses.meaning: The self, blinded by ego, thinks 'I am the doer.' But nature's qualities perform every deed.
verses.takeaway: You are not the author you think you are.

verses.devanagari:
प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः ।
अहंकारविमूढात्मा कर्ताहमिति मन्यते
verses.iast:
prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ |
ahaṃkāravimūḍhātmā kartāhamiti manyate
verses.meaning: But one who knows the truth stays unattached. It is only qualities playing among qualities.
verses.takeaway: Watch the play instead of grabbing the pieces.

verses.devanagari:
तत्त्ववित्तु महाबाहो गुणकर्मविभागयोः ।
गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते
verses.iast:
tattvavittu mahābāho guṇakarmavibhāgayoḥ |
guṇā guṇeṣu vartanta iti matvā na sajjate
verses.meaning: Those fooled by nature's qualities cling to its workings. The wise must not unsettle such half-knowing, slow minds.
verses.takeaway: Meet people inside their picture before redrawing it.

verses.devanagari:
प्रकृतेर्गुणसंमूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु ।
तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दान्कृत्स्नविन्न विचालयेत्
verses.iast:
prakṛterguṇasaṃmūḍhāḥ sajjante guṇakarmasu |
tānakṛtsnavido mandānkṛtsnavinna vicālayet
verses.meaning: Hand all your actions to Me, mind fixed on the self, free of hope and ego. Then fight, your fever gone.
verses.takeaway: Surrender the results, keep the sword.

verses.devanagari:
मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा ।
निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः
verses.iast:
mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasyādhyātmacetasā |
nirāśīrnirmamo bhūtvā yudhyasva vigatajvaraḥ
verses.meaning: Dedicate all your actions to Me, mind anchored in the highest self. Fight free of hope, of mine-ness, of fever.
verses.takeaway: Three poisons out, one sword in hand.

verses.devanagari:
ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः ।
श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्मभिः
verses.iast:
ye me matamidaṃ nityamanutiṣṭhanti mānavāḥ |
śraddhāvanto'nasūyanto mucyante te'pi karmabhiḥ
verses.meaning: Those who live by this teaching of Mine, full of faith and free of nitpicking — they are freed from the bonds of action.
verses.takeaway: Trust plus practice beats analysis alone.

verses.devanagari:
ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम् ।
सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः
verses.iast:
ye tvetadabhyasūyanto nānutiṣṭhanti me matam |
sarvajñānavimūḍhāṃstānviddhi naṣṭānacetasaḥ
verses.meaning: But those who sneer at My teaching and ignore it are senseless, confused in all knowledge, and lost.
verses.takeaway: The teaching warns about rejecting the teaching. Noted.

verses.devanagari:
सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि ।
प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति
verses.iast:
sadṛśaṃ ceṣṭate svasyāḥ prakṛterjñānavānapi |
prakṛtiṃ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati
verses.meaning: Even the wise act according to their nature. All beings follow nature — what can repression do?
verses.takeaway: Work with your nature, not against it.

verses.devanagari:
इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ ।
तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ
verses.iast:
indriyasyendriyasyārthe rāgadveṣau vyavasthitau |
tayorna vaśamāgacchettau hyasya paripanthinau
verses.meaning: Every sense has its likes and dislikes toward its objects. Never bow to either — both are your enemies on the path.
verses.takeaway: Your preferences are not your friends.

verses.devanagari:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् ।
स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः
verses.iast:
śreyānsvadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmātsvanuṣṭhitāt |
svadharme nidhanaṃ śreyaḥ paradharmo bhayāvahaḥ
verses.meaning: Your own duty, done badly, beats another's duty done well. Death in your own duty is fine; a borrowed path is perilous.
verses.takeaway: Stay in your lane — gloriously.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन
verses.devanagari:
अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः ।
अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः
verses.iast:
atha kena prayukto'yaṃ pāpaṃ carati pūruṣaḥ |
anicchannapi vārṣṇeya balādiva niyojitaḥ
verses.meaning: Arjuna said: but what drives a person to sin, Krishna, even unwillingly, as if dragged by force?
verses.takeaway: The oldest question in the book, asked plainly.

verses.devanagari:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः ।
महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम्
verses.iast:
śrībhagavānuvāca
kāma eṣa krodha eṣa rajoguṇasamudbhavaḥ |
mahāśano mahāpāpmā viddhyenamiha vairiṇam
verses.meaning: Krishna said: it is desire, it is anger — born of passion, all-devouring, terribly sinful. Know it as the enemy here.
verses.takeaway: Name the enemy: wanting.

verses.devanagari:
धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथादर्शो मलेन च ।
यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम्
verses.iast:
dhūmenāvriyate vahniryathādarśo malena ca |
yatholbenāvṛto garbhastathā tenedamāvṛtam
verses.meaning: As fire is veiled by smoke, a mirror by dust, a baby by the womb — so wisdom is veiled by desire.
verses.takeaway: Three pictures for one blindness.

verses.devanagari:
आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा ।
कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च
verses.iast:
āvṛtaṃ jñānametena jñānino nityavairiṇā |
kāmarūpeṇa kaunteya duṣpūreṇānalena ca
verses.meaning: Wisdom is smothered by this eternal enemy of the wise. Desire burns like fire. It is never satisfied.
verses.takeaway: Insatiable is the scariest word here.

verses.devanagari:
इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते ।
एतैर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम्
verses.iast:
indriyāṇi mano buddhirasyādhiṣṭhānamucyate |
etairvimohayatyeṣa jñānamāvṛtya dehinam
verses.meaning: The senses, the mind and understanding are its home. Through them desire confuses the embodied self, veiling wisdom.
verses.takeaway: Know where the enemy lives.

verses.devanagari:
तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ ।
पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम्
verses.iast:
tasmāttvamindriyāṇyādau niyamya bharatarṣabha |
pāpmānaṃ prajahi hyenaṃ jñānavijñānanāśanam
verses.meaning: So first rein in the senses, Arjuna, then strike down this evil thing that murders wisdom and learning.
verses.takeaway: Gates first, fortress second.

verses.devanagari:
इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः ।
मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः
verses.iast:
indriyāṇi parāṇyāhurindriyebhyaḥ paraṃ manaḥ |
manasastu parā buddhiryo buddheḥ paratastu saḥ
verses.meaning: The senses are great. Greater than the senses is the mind. Greater than the mind is understanding. And greater than understanding is That.
verses.takeaway: Climb the ladder rung by rung.

verses.devanagari:
एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना ।
जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम्
verses.iast:
evaṃ buddheḥ paraṃ buddhvā saṃstabhyātmānamātmanā |
jahi śatruṃ mahābāho kāmarūpaṃ durāsadam
verses.meaning: Know That which lies beyond understanding. Steady yourself by yourself. And destroy this elusive enemy called desire.
verses.takeaway: Last word of the chapter: destroy it.

verses.devanagari: विवस्वान्मनवे प्राह मनुरिक्ष्वाकवेऽब्रवीत्
verses.iast: vivasvānmanave prāha manurikṣvākave'bravīt
verses.meaning: Krishna said: this timeless discipline I taught to the sun-god long ago. He taught Manu, and Manu taught Ikshvaku.
verses.takeaway: Wisdom travels teacher to student, age to age.

verses.devanagari:
एवं परम्पराप्राप्तमिमं राजर्षयो विदुः ।
स कालेनेह महता योगो नष्टः परन्तप
verses.iast:
evaṃ paramparāprāptamimaṃ rājarṣayo viduḥ |
sa kāleneha mahatā yogo naṣṭaḥ parantapa
verses.meaning: Passed down this way, kings and sages knew it. But over long time, Arjuna, this discipline faded from the world.
verses.takeaway: Even the best teachings need retelling.

verses.devanagari:
स एवायं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः ।
भक्तोऽसि मे सखा चेति रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम्
verses.iast:
sa evāyaṃ mayā te'dya yogaḥ proktaḥ purātanaḥ |
bhakto'si me sakhā ceti rahasyaṃ hyetaduttamam
verses.meaning: That same ancient discipline I teach you today. Because you are my devotee and my friend. And this is the deepest secret.
verses.takeaway: Truth goes to the ready heart.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन
verses.devanagari:
अपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वतः ।
कथमेतद्विजानीयां त्वमादौ प्रोक्तवानिति
verses.iast:
aparaṃ bhavato janma paraṃ janma vivasvataḥ |
kathametadvijānīyāṃ tvamādau proktavāniti
verses.meaning: Arjuna said: you were born later, and the sun was born long before. How am I to understand that you taught this first?
verses.takeaway: A fair question deserves a straight answer.

verses.devanagari:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
बहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन ।
तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप
verses.iast:
śrībhagavānuvāca
bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava cārjuna |
tānyahaṃ veda sarvāṇi na tvaṃ vettha parantapa
verses.meaning: Krishna said: I have lived through many births, Arjuna, and so have you. I remember them all. You do not.
verses.takeaway: Memory is the difference between you and Me. For now.

verses.devanagari:
अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा भूतानामीश्वरोऽपि सन् ।
प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्ठाय संभवाम्यात्ममायया
verses.iast:
ajo'pi sannavyayātmā bhūtānāmīśvaro'pi san |
prakṛtiṃ svāmadhiṣṭhāya saṃbhavāmyātmamāyayā
verses.meaning: Though I am unborn and undying in my being. Though I am lord of all creatures. I take charge of my own nature. And I am born — by my own power of illusion.
verses.takeaway: The unlimited puts on limits, on purpose.

verses.devanagari:
यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत ।
अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम्
verses.iast:
yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata |
abhyutthānamadharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmyaham
verses.meaning: Whenever goodness fades, Arjuna, and evil rises up — then I make Myself.
verses.takeaway: Help arrives on schedule: when things are worst.

verses.devanagari:
परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् ।
धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे
verses.iast:
paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām |
dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge
verses.meaning: Age after age I am born — to guard the good, destroy the wicked, and set goodness firmly back in place.
verses.takeaway: The most quoted promise in the book.

verses.devanagari:
जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ।
त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्जुन
verses.iast:
janma karma ca me divyamevaṃ yo vetti tattvataḥ |
tyaktvā dehaṃ punarjanma naiti māmeti so'rjuna
verses.meaning: Whoever truly knows My divine birth and work like this leaves the body and is never born again. Such a one comes to Me.
verses.takeaway: Know it for real, and you are free.

verses.devanagari:
वीतरागभयक्रोधा मन्मया मामुपाश्रिताः ।
बहवो ज्ञानतपसा पूता मद्भावमागताः
verses.iast:
vītarāgabhayakrodhā manmayā māmupāśritāḥ |
bahavo jñānatapasā pūtā madbhāvamāgatāḥ
verses.meaning: Freed from craving, fear, and anger. Filled with Me. Depending on Me. Purified by the fire of wisdom. Many have entered into My being.
verses.takeaway: The entry requirements, stated plainly.

verses.devanagari:
ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम् ।
मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः
verses.iast:
ye yathā māṃ prapadyante tāṃstathaiva bhajāmyaham |
mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ
verses.meaning: However people approach Me, I meet them that way. All paths lead to Me in the end, Arjuna.
verses.takeaway: Every sincere road arrives.

verses.devanagari:
काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः ।
क्षिप्रं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्भवति कर्मजा
verses.iast:
kāṅkṣantaḥ karmaṇāṃ siddhiṃ yajanta iha devatāḥ |
kṣipraṃ hi mānuṣe loke siddhirbhavati karmajā
verses.meaning: Wanting their actions to pay off, people worship the gods here — because in this human world, results come fast.
verses.takeaway: Impatience explains most worship.

verses.devanagari:
चातुर्वर्ण्यं मया सृष्टं गुणकर्मविभागशः ।
तस्य कर्तारमपि मां विद्ध्यकर्तारमव्ययम्
verses.iast:
cāturvarṇyaṃ mayā sṛṣṭaṃ guṇakarmavibhāgaśaḥ |
tasya kartāramapi māṃ viddhyakartāramavyayam
verses.meaning: The fourfold social order I created, matching inborn nature to work. And though I made it, know Me as the changeless non-maker.
verses.takeaway: Made the system, stands outside it.

verses.devanagari:
न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा ।
इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते
verses.iast:
na māṃ karmāṇi limpanti na me karmaphale spṛhā |
iti māṃ yo'bhijānāti karmabhirna sa badhyate
verses.meaning: Actions do not stain Me. I hunger for no fruits of action. Whoever knows Me this way is not chained by deeds.
verses.takeaway: Do the work. Skip the hunger.

verses.devanagari:
एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः ।
कुरु कर्मैव तस्मात्त्वं पूर्वैः पूर्वतरं कृतम्
verses.iast:
evaṃ jñātvā kṛtaṃ karma pūrvairapi mumukṣubhiḥ |
kuru karmaiva tasmāttvaṃ pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraṃ kṛtam
verses.meaning: Knowing this, even the ancient seekers of freedom did their work. So you too — act, as the ancients acted in olden times.
verses.takeaway: Precedent matters. Follow the ones who got free.

verses.devanagari:
किं कर्म किमकर्मेति कवयोऽप्यत्र मोहिताः ।
तत्ते कर्म प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात्
verses.iast:
kiṃ karma kimakarmeti kavayo'pyatra mohitāḥ |
tatte karma pravakṣyāmi yajjñātvā mokṣyase'śubhāt
verses.meaning: Even the wise get confused about what action is and what inaction is. I will explain action to you — knowing it, you will escape evil.
verses.takeaway: If the wise get confused, beginners may ask.

verses.devanagari:
कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः ।
अकर्मणश्च बोद्धव्यं गहना कर्मणो गतिः
verses.iast:
karmaṇo hyapi boddhavyaṃ boddhavyaṃ ca vikarmaṇaḥ |
akarmaṇaśca boddhavyaṃ gahanā karmaṇo gatiḥ
verses.meaning: You must understand action, and forbidden action, and inaction too. The truth about action runs very deep.
verses.takeaway: Three things to learn, not one.

verses.devanagari:
कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः ।
स बुद्धिमान्मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत्
verses.iast:
karmaṇyakarma yaḥ paśyedakarmaṇi ca karma yaḥ |
sa buddhimānmanuṣyeṣu sa yuktaḥ kṛtsnakarmakṛt
verses.meaning: Whoever sees inaction in action, and action in inaction — that person is wise. Disciplined. Doing every deed fully.
verses.takeaway: The riddle at the heart of the chapter.

verses.devanagari:
यस्य सर्वे समारम्भाः कामसंकल्पवर्जिताः ।
ज्ञानाग्निदग्धकर्माणं तमाहुः पण्डितं बुधाः
verses.iast:
yasya sarve samārambhāḥ kāmasaṃkalpavarjitāḥ |
jñānāgnidagdhakarmāṇaṃ tamāhuḥ paṇḍitaṃ budhāḥ
verses.meaning: The wise call learned the one whose every act is free of selfish desire. Free of planning. Whose deeds are burned up in the fire of wisdom.
verses.takeaway: Burn the motive, keep the motion.

verses.devanagari:
त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः ।
कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किंचित्करोति सः
verses.iast:
tyaktvā karmaphalāsaṅgaṃ nityatṛpto nirāśrayaḥ |
karmaṇyabhipravṛtto'pi naiva kiṃcitkaroti saḥ
verses.meaning: Dropping clinging to results. Always content. Needing nothing. Such a one does nothing at all — even while acting hard.
verses.takeaway: The busiest idleness and idlest busyness meet here.

verses.devanagari:
निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः ।
शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्
verses.iast:
nirāśīryatacittātmā tyaktasarvaparigrahaḥ |
śārīraṃ kevalaṃ karma kurvannāpnoti kilbiṣam
verses.meaning: Expecting nothing. Mind and self controlled. Owning nothing. One incurs no wrong by acting merely to keep the body going.
verses.takeaway: Act for upkeep, not for hunger.

verses.devanagari:
यदृच्छालाभसंतुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः ।
समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते
verses.iast:
yadṛcchālābhasaṃtuṣṭo dvandvātīto vimatsaraḥ |
samaḥ siddhāvasiddhau ca kṛtvāpi na nibadhyate
verses.meaning: Content with whatever comes on its own. Beyond opposites. Free of envy. Steady in success and failure. Such a one is never chained, however hard one acts.
verses.takeaway: Contentment is the only wealth that compounds.

verses.devanagari:
गतसङ्गस्य मुक्तस्य ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः ।
यज्ञायाचरतः कर्म समग्रं प्रविलीयते
verses.iast:
gatasaṅgasya muktasya jñānāvasthitacetasaḥ |
yajñāyācarataḥ karma samagraṃ pravilīyate
verses.meaning: For one free of clinging. Liberated. Mind anchored in wisdom. Acting only as offering. Every deed fully dissolves.
verses.takeaway: Offer it up and watch it dissolve.

verses.devanagari:
ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्म हविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम् ।
ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना
verses.iast:
brahmārpaṇaṃ brahma havirbrahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam |
brahmaiva tena gantavyaṃ brahmakarmasamādhinā
verses.meaning: The offering is ultimate reality. The offered, into its fire. Ultimate reality is the goal — for one absorbed in it through action.
verses.takeaway: All sacred, all the way down.

verses.devanagari:
दैवमेवापरे यज्ञं योगिनः पर्युपासते ।
ब्रह्माग्नावपरे यज्ञं यज्ञेनैवोपजुह्वति
verses.iast:
daivamevāpare yajñaṃ yoginaḥ paryupāsate |
brahmāgnāvapare yajñaṃ yajñenaivopajuhvati
verses.meaning: Some worship the gods with offerings. Others offer the act itself into ultimate reality's fire.
verses.takeaway: Many altars, one fire.

verses.devanagari:
श्रोत्रादीनीन्द्रियाण्यन्ये संयमाग्निषु जुह्वति ।
शब्दादीन्विषयानन्य इन्द्रियाग्निषु जुह्वति
verses.iast:
śrotrādīnīndriyāṇyanye saṃyamāgniṣu juhvati |
śabdādīnviṣayānanya indriyāgniṣu juhvati
verses.meaning: Others offer hearing and the rest of the senses into the fires of restraint. Others offer sights and sounds into the fires of the senses.
verses.takeaway: Everything can be fuel, aimed right.

verses.devanagari:
सर्वाणीन्द्रियकर्माणि प्राणकर्माणि चापरे ।
आत्मसंयमयोगाग्नौ जुह्वति ज्ञानदीपिते
verses.iast:
sarvāṇīndriyakarmāṇi prāṇakarmāṇi cāpare |
ātmasaṃyamayogāgnau juhvati jñānadīpite
verses.meaning: Others offer every sense-act into the fire of self-restraint. And every breath. Lit by wisdom.
verses.takeaway: The inward sacrifice needs no temple.

verses.devanagari:
द्रव्ययज्ञास्तपोयज्ञा योगयज्ञास्तथापरे ।
स्वाध्यायज्ञानयज्ञाश्च यतयः संशितव्रताः
verses.iast:
dravyayajñāstapoyajñā yogayajñāstathāpare |
svādhyāyajñānayajñāśca yatayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ
verses.meaning: Others offer wealth. Or penance. Or focus, study, wisdom. Ascetics of strict vows.
verses.takeaway: Give what you have. It counts.

verses.devanagari:
अपाने जुह्वति प्राणं प्राणेऽपानं तथापरे ।
प्राणापानगती रुद्ध्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः
verses.iast:
apāne juhvati prāṇaṃ prāṇe'pānaṃ tathāpare |
prāṇāpānagatī ruddhvā prāṇāyāmaparāyaṇāḥ
verses.meaning: Others, eating little, pour one breath into another, then hold both still — devoted to breath control.
verses.takeaway: The body itself becomes the altar.

verses.devanagari:
अपरे नियताहाराः प्राणान्प्राणेषु जुह्वति ।
सर्वेऽप्येते यज्ञविदो यज्ञक्षपितकल्मषाः
verses.iast:
apare niyatāhārāḥ prāṇānprāṇeṣu juhvati |
sarve'pyete yajñavido yajñakṣapitakalmaṣāḥ
verses.meaning: All of these know sacrifice, and sacrifice burns away their wrongs.
verses.takeaway: Every sincere method works. Pick one and mean it.

verses.devanagari:
यज्ञशिष्टामृतभुजो यान्ति ब्रह्म सनातनम् ।
नायं लोकोऽस्त्ययज्ञस्य कुतोऽन्यः कुरुसत्तम
verses.iast:
yajñaśiṣṭāmṛtabhujo yānti brahma sanātanam |
nāyaṃ loko'styayajñasya kuto'nyaḥ kurusattama
verses.meaning: Those who taste the nectar left from sacrifice reach the eternal ultimate reality. This world is not for the non-sacrificer — how then the next?
verses.takeaway: You cannot skip giving and arrive at having.

verses.devanagari:
एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे ।
कर्मजान्विद्धि तान्सर्वानेवं ज्ञात्वा विमोक्ष्यसे
verses.iast:
evaṃ bahuvidhā yajñā vitatā brahmaṇo mukhe |
karmajānviddhi tānsarvānevaṃ jñātvā vimokṣyase
verses.meaning: So sacrifices of many kinds lie spread in the Vedas. Know them all born of action — and knowing this, you will be free.
verses.takeaway: Map the territory, then walk out of it.

verses.devanagari:
श्रेयान्द्रव्यमयाद्यज्ञाज्ज्ञानयज्ञः परन्तप ।
सर्वं कर्माखिलं पार्थ ज्ञाने परिसमाप्यते
verses.iast:
śreyāndravyamayādyajñājjñānayajñaḥ parantapa |
sarvaṃ karmākhilaṃ pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate
verses.meaning: The sacrifice of wisdom beats any gift of wealth. Every action is fully contained in wisdom.
verses.takeaway: Understanding outranks offerings.

verses.devanagari:
तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया ।
उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः
verses.iast:
tadviddhi praṇipātena paripraśnena sevayā |
upadekṣyanti te jñānaṃ jñāninastattvadarśinaḥ
verses.meaning: Learn it by bowing down, by asking, by serving. Those who see truth will teach you wisdom.
verses.takeaway: The student contract: humility, questions, service.

verses.devanagari:
यज्ज्ञात्वा न पुनर्मोहमेवं यास्यसि पाण्डव ।
येन भूतान्यशेषेण द्रक्ष्यस्यात्मन्यथो मयि
verses.iast:
yajjñātvā na punarmohamevaṃ yāsyasi pāṇḍava |
yena bhūtānyaśeṣeṇa drakṣyasyātmanyatho mayi
verses.meaning: Learning it, you will never fall into this confusion again. Through it you will see all beings — every one — first in yourself, then in Me.
verses.takeaway: Other people are yourself, wearing different faces.

verses.devanagari:
अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः ।
सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि
verses.iast:
api cedasi pāpebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpakṛttamaḥ |
sarvaṃ jñānaplavenaiva vṛjinaṃ santariṣyasi
verses.meaning: Even if you are the worst sinner alive, you will cross all wrongdoing on the raft of wisdom alone.
verses.takeaway: No one is past rescuing. No one.

verses.devanagari:
यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्जुन ।
ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा
verses.iast:
yathaidhāṃsi samiddho'gnirbhasmasātkurute'rjuna |
jñānāgniḥ sarvakarmāṇi bhasmasātkurute tathā
verses.meaning: As a blazing fire turns fuel to ash, so wisdom's fire turns all actions to ash.
verses.takeaway: The second great fire image — it returns because it works.

verses.devanagari:
न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते ।
तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति
verses.iast:
na hi jñānena sadṛśaṃ pavitramiha vidyate |
tatsvayaṃ yogasaṃsiddhaḥ kālenātmani vindati
verses.meaning: Nothing purifies in this world like wisdom. In time, the self, perfected in discipline, finds it within.
verses.takeaway: The treasure was inside the house all along.

verses.devanagari:
श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः ।
ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति
verses.iast:
śraddhāvām̐llabhate jñānaṃ tatparaḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ |
jñānaṃ labdhvā parāṃ śāntimacireṇādhigacchati
verses.meaning: The faithful one, senses restrained, devoted — gains wisdom. Gaining wisdom, one soon reaches supreme peace.
verses.takeaway: Faith, focus, devotion: the three keys on one ring.

verses.devanagari:
अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति ।
नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः
verses.iast:
ajñaścāśraddadhānaśca saṃśayātmā vinaśyati |
nāyaṃ loko'sti na paro na sukhaṃ saṃśayātmanaḥ
verses.meaning: The ignorant, the faithless, the doubting self destroys itself. Neither this world nor the next — nor any happiness — belongs to the doubter.
verses.takeaway: Doubt, not failure, is the dead end.

verses.devanagari:
योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसंछिन्नसंशयम् ।
आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनंजय
verses.iast:
yogasaṃnyastakarmāṇaṃ jñānasaṃchinnasaṃśayam |
ātmavantaṃ na karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanaṃjaya
